sources.entry: 1. Attack Surface Analysis Cheat Sheet by OWASP

summary.title: Attack Surface Analysis Cheat Sheet
summary.one_liner: You learn a pragmatic method for mapping an application's entry and exit points, classifying and measuring its attack surface, and tracking how changes to the system alter risk.
takeaways: The attack surface is the set of data/command paths into and out of an application, the code protecting them, and the valuable data it handles.
Group attack points into buckets by type and count them, then sample cases for review instead of examining every endpoint.
Prioritize remote, internet-facing and anonymous entry points, plus authentication, crypto and access-control code.
Re-assess the attack surface when session management, authorization, secrets handling, or architecture changes; reduce it by removing unused features and data.
summary.summary: This OWASP cheat sheet explains Attack Surface Analysis as a practical way to map where attackers could get data into or out of an application and which areas need security review. It walks through defining the attack surface, identifying entry points such as UI forms, headers, APIs, files and databases, and grouping them into risk buckets. It also covers microservice and cloud-native considerations, measurement approaches like RSQ and a CMU attack surface metric, and how to manage changes over time. The focus is on external attack, with guidance aimed at developers and security specialists.
